newsitem.title: USA: MOODY'S CUTS PROVIDIAN FINANCIAL RATING.
newsitem.headline: MOODY'S CUTS PROVIDIAN FINANCIAL RATING.

text.p: NEW YORK, June 12 - Moody's Investors Service downgraded the ratings of Providian Financial Corporation (formerly Providian Bancorp, Inc.) and its bank subsidiaries First Deposit National Bank and Providian National Bank.
The rating agency's actions follow the June 10, 1997 spin-off of Providian Financial Corporation as an independent, publicly-held company.
Providian Financial was previously a wholly-owned subsidiary of Providian Corporation (senior at A2), a diversified insurance company.

The ratings were placed on review for possible downgrade on December 30, 1996 following the announcement by Providian Corporation that it intended to spin off Providian Financial in connection with the sale of Providian Corporation's insurance operations to Aegon N.V. Providian Financial, through its bank subsidiaries, is primarily an unsecured credit card lender, and engages to a lesser degree in secured credit card and home equity lending.

Moody's said the downgrade reflects the largely monoline nature of the company, the highly competitive nature of the credit card industry, the company's heavy and increasing reliance upon securitization as a principal source of financing, and the risks inherent in management's aggressive growth projections and capital management policies.

These factors are likely to weaken the company's historically strong financials, the rating agency noted, and as the company grows it will become more difficult to preserve its relatively unique marketing position.

In addition, Providian Financial and its bank subsidiaries are no longer able to rely upon Providian Corporation for any support. Providian Financial has a highly focused strategy targeting high balance revolvers, the rating agency noted, that has resulted in significantly higher net interest margins than its peers but has also resulted in above-average credit costs.
Although the company's management and underwriting are strong, the company has not been immune to the negative trends affecting the rest of the credit card industry.

Following the spin-off, the company's management team will remain in place. Moody's also said that the rating outlook for Providian Financial's smaller bank subsidiary, Providian National Bank, is negative. Providian National Bank was established in 1990 to allow the company more flexibility in managing the assets of its lead bank, First Deposit National Bank.

At that time, First Deposit could not legally grow faster than seven percent per year. However, in September 1996 this legal asset growth restriction on First Deposit was lifted, eliminating the strategic need for Providian National Bank.
Since that time almost no new accounts have been booked at Providian National Bank, its provisions for loan losses have declined significantly, and its capital levels have been reduced.
Because of these factors and the lack of strategic importance of Providian National Bank to the company, Moody's is placing a negative outlook on the ratings for Providian National Bank.
The company is reviewing strategic alternatives for Providian National Bank, including merging it with First Deposit National Bank.
The rating outlooks for Providian Financial Corporation and First Deposit National Bank are stable.
The following ratings were downgraded: Providian Financial Corporation -- the rating for junior subordinated debt to Ba3 from Baa1.
Providian Bancorp Capital Trust I -- the preferred stock rating for the trust's Capital Securities to "ba3" from "baa1."

First Deposit National Bank -- the rating of the bank for long-term deposits to Baa2 from A2; the rating for other long term senior obligations to Baa3 from A2; the counterparty rating to Baa3 from A2; the ratings of the bank for short-term deposits and other senior obligations to Prime-3 from Prime-1; and the Bank Financial Strength Rating to D+ from C.

Providian National Bank -- the rating of the bank for long-term deposits to Baa2 from A2; the rating for other long term senior obligations to Baa3 from A2; the counterparty rating to Baa3 from A2; the ratings of the bank for short-term deposits and other senior obligations to Prime-3 from Prime-1; and the Bank Financial Strength Rating to D from D+.

As of March 31, 1997, Providian Financial Corporation, headquartered in San Francisco, California, had total assets under management of $10.6 billion and ranked as the 15th largest credit card issuer in the United States.

First Deposit National Bank, Tilton, New Hampshire, had total assets under management of $7.3 billion and Providian National Bank, Concord, New Hampshire, had total assets under management of $3.2 billion. Thursday, 12 June 1997 16:49:59
